settings.whereArcGetsDetails: Provider credentials for title details and artwork. Library metadata options are under Manage libraries.
settings.moviesAndShows: Movie and TV details and artwork. Requires a TMDB API key.
settings.showsAndTheirEpisode: TV details and episode orders. Requires a TheTVDB API key with access for your project.
settings.scoresFromOtherSites: Additional ratings shown on title pages and available when sorting your library.
settings.criticsScoresFromOmdb: Adds Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic ratings through OMDb. Availability and request limits depend on your API access.
settings.howArcFindsNew: How Arc finds new and changed files. Applies to every library.
settings.pickUpNewAnd: Scan when Arc detects new or changed files. Some network drives do not report changes.
settings.regularlyCheckEveryFolder: How often Arc checks every library folder for new, changed or missing files. Existing matches are reused.
settings.librariesUpdateWhenYou: Automatic, scheduled and startup scans are off. Scan a library manually to check for changes.
settings.fullScansAreOff: Scheduled scans are off. Detected file changes and startup scans are still enabled.
settings.fullScansAreOff2: Scheduled scans are off. Detected file changes still trigger scans.
settings.fullScansAreOff3: Scheduled scans are off. Startup scans are still enabled.
settings.whenAChangeIs: When a change is detected, check just that folder instead of the whole library.
settings.checkEveryLibraryFor: Check every library for changes when Arc starts.
settings.bringEveryoneSWatch: Import watch history and supported lists from Plex or Jellyfin. Choose how users map to Arc profiles.
settings.watchedStatusResumePoints: Watched status, resume points, ratings and history for everyone, plus your watchlist, playlists and collections.
settings.watchedStatusAndResume: Watched status, resume points, favourites and playlists for every user, plus collections. Needs an administrator sign-in.
settings.sendMessagesToDiscord: Send selected server events to Discord, Slack or another webhook address.
settings.ffmpegReadsYourVideo: ffprobe reads media details. FFmpeg converts video and generates media assets when needed.
settings.whereSkipIntroRecap: Where Skip Intro, Recap and Credits come from. Each library chooses whether to offer them.
settings.chaptersNamedOpeningOr: Chapters named Opening or Ending, then IntroDB, a free community database. No key needed.
settings.aLargerCommunityDatabase: An additional source of intro, recap and credit markers, checked before IntroDB when a key is configured.
settings.aShortClipPlayed: A short clip played before movies, like a cinema intro or a trailer.
settings.findSubtitlesOnlineFrom: Find subtitles online from the player when a video doesn't have the ones you want.
settings.whenADeviceCan: When a device can't play a file as it is, Arc converts it while it's watched.
settings.noSupportedGraphicsCard: No supported hardware encoder is available. Arc uses the CPU for video conversion.
settings.thisFfmpegCanT: This FFmpeg build does not support HDR-to-SDR tone mapping. Converted HDR video may display incorrect colours.
settings.keepConvertedHdrVideo: Convert HDR colours to SDR when a video needs conversion for an SDR screen.
settings.howManyVideosArc: Maximum concurrent video conversions. Direct Play and streams that only repackage the file do not count.
settings.easyToPlayCopies: Easy-to-play copies made ahead of time, used instead of converting while you watch.
settings.awayFromHomeThe: Password-free profile selection applies only to your Home networks.
settings.atHomePeopleJust: At home, people just pick a profile. The admin profile still needs the password or its PIN.
settings.letPhonesTvsAnd: Let phones, TVs and other computers on your network use Arc.
settings.watchAwayFromHome: Configure access from outside your home network. Router or reverse-proxy setup may also be needed.
settings.biggerVideosAreConverted: Compatible videos within this bitrate and resolution limit keep their original quality. Others may need conversion.
settings.browsersAndAppsSigned: Browsers and apps signed in to Arc. Sign out any you don't recognise.
settings.heavyWorkWaitsFor: Choose when scheduled background tasks may run. Some tasks wait while playback or scanning is active.
settings.tasksCanRunAt: Scheduled tasks may run at any time of day, when their other requirements are met.
settings.tasksRunBetweenThese: Scheduled tasks use these hours in the server's time zone. Unfinished work can continue in a later window.
settings.informationToHelpWhen: Information to help when something is slow or goes wrong.
settings.filesOrFoldersOne: Video files or folders on the server, one per line. Played when a movie starts from the beginning, not when resuming. MP4 with H.264 offers broad compatibility.
settings.optionalSigningInAllows: Optional: signing in allows more downloads a day.
settings.whereVideoIsKept: Temporary files used during video conversion. Click to choose a folder. Use Default clears the custom path and uses Arc's data folder.
settings.ffmpegFoundFilesA: FFmpeg found: files a browser can’t play are converted as they’re watched
settings.ffmpegWasnTFound: FFmpeg wasn’t found next to ffprobe, so files a browser can’t play won’t be converted
settings.hardwareDescription: Use {{hardware}} for supported video conversions. Arc can fall back to the CPU when needed.
settings.serverNameHint: How Arc's apps and sign-in pages name this server, e.g. “Living Room”. Up to 80 characters.

diagnostics.recordExtraDetailFor: Record extra detail for troubleshooting. Turns off automatically after 2 hours.
diagnostics.recentLogsSurviveRestarts: Recent logs survive restarts. Arc keeps up to three 2 MB log files.
diagnostics.recentLogsAreAvailable: Recent logs are available for this session only.
diagnostics.recentLogsAndBuild: Recent logs, build details, active request stages and runtime call stacks, with passwords and keys removed. Names and file paths may be included.
diagnostics.everyRequestThisServer: API reference for building apps and scripts that connect to Arc.

webhooks.showingTheLastLoaded: Showing the last loaded notifications. They may be out of date.
webhooks.loadNotificationsBeforeAdding: Load notifications before adding a webhook.
webhooks.arcPostsAMessage: Arc posts a message to this address when the events you choose happen.
webhooks.discordAndSlackAddresses: Discord and Slack addresses get a tidy message; anything else gets the event as JSON.
webhooks.name: Name
webhooks.addDescription: Add a Discord or Slack webhook, or any address that accepts JSON (like ntfy or home automation).

scheduledWork.accepted: Run requested. Progress and the result will appear here.

emptyTrashTask.afterEachCompleteScan: During maintenance, Arc can remove database records for files no longer present after a complete scan. Watch history for removed titles is lost. Leave this off if you disconnect drives temporarily.
emptyTrashTask.itOnlyRunsWhen: It only runs when every library folder could be read, and saves a backup first. Your media files are never deleted.
emptyTrashTask.runAllExplanation: Check all libraries and remove database records for files no longer present. Watch history and edits for removed titles are lost. Media files are never deleted. This does not change the automatic-cleanup setting.
emptyTrashTask.runAllSafety: Each library needs a fresh complete scan, unchanged readable folders and a known present file in each folder. Busy or unsafe libraries are skipped. A safety backup must succeed before any removal.
emptyTrashTask.runningAll: Checking libraries one at a time…
emptyTrashTask.busyLibrary: Skipped: library work is running. Retry when it finishes.
emptyTrashTask.scanRequired: Skipped: run a complete scan and check that all folders are online, then retry. An entirely empty folder needs individual confirmation in Manage libraries.
emptyTrashTask.runningLibrary: Checking folders and backing up before cleanup…

emptyTrash.removeTitlesWhoseFiles: Remove titles whose files are gone?
emptyTrash.onlyDoThisIf: Only do this if the files are gone for good, not on a disconnected drive. A backup is made first. Media files are never deleted.
emptyTrash.explanation: Arc removes missing-file records in {{name}}, then removes any movie, episode or show left with no files, including its watch history. Titles with another file are kept. Media files are never deleted.

tasks.previewsDescription: Pictures shown while dragging along the timeline, for libraries that have them turned on.
tasks.markersDescription: Finds intros by comparing a season’s episodes, and movie end credits, when nothing is found online.
tasks.analysisDescription: Brings older files up to date when Arc learns to read more from them, such as Dolby Vision, HDR10+ and Atmos. New files are analysed when added.
tasks.metadataDescription: Keeps titles’ details and artwork up to date, more often for shows that are still airing.
tasks.backupDescription: Daily database backups during maintenance. You can also back up any time in Backups & restore.
tasks.databaseDescription: Checks and optimises the database during maintenance, normally once a week.
tasks.cacheDescription: Weekly removal of cached images, previews and subtitles nothing uses any more. Your media files are never touched.
tasks.emptyTrashDescription: During maintenance, removes records for missing files after a complete scan. Watch history for removed titles is lost. Leave it off if drives may be disconnected. Media files stay untouched.

events.problem: Problems, like a failed scan or backup

detectionHelp.off: Automatic local detection is off. Markers from chapters and online providers can still be used.
detectionHelp.scheduled: During maintenance, compares a season's episodes for intros and detects movie end credits when no markers are found online.
detectionHelp.added: After import and during maintenance, compares a season's episodes for intros and detects movie end credits when no markers are found online.
